text:
Alex Kim: thinking about how we encode SLO-driven routing + circuit-breakers for customer tiers. do we want a single policy DSL or layered rules (tier -> region -> model-variant)?
Priya Rao: single DSL with clear precedence would be nicer for the UI, but need expressive predicates for latency/availability SLOs.
Marco Díaz: agree. also need the ability to express emergency fallbacks: e.g. when p95 > 300ms for tier=gold in eu-west, route to quantized-variant or lower-cost region.
Jen Liu: +1. also quota interactions: if reserved capacity is exhausted, we should soft-fail to best-effort path rather than hard-block. users want graceful degradation.
Alex Kim: sketching a tiny example DSL: ```policy: - when: tier == "gold" and region == "eu-west-1"   slo: {p95_latency_ms: 300, availability_pct: 99.9}   fallback: [quantized-v2, other-region]   cb: {window_sec: 60, error_rate_pct: 5}```
Priya Rao: that looks good. two questions: 1) do we let fallback be prioritized list or weighted? 2) how do we surface telemetry to validate the condition (p95 computed per minute vs rolling)?
Marco Díaz: prioritized list is simpler to reason about for rollout UX. weights could be added later. For telemetry, we should define aggregation window (e.g. rolling 5m) and a signal name: `routing.slo.p95_ms` and `routing.slo.availability_pct`.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] policy-schema v2 pushed to staging.
Jen Liu: UX concern: in the console we show an effective policy for a customer (after merging defaults + overrides). we should display the recent SLO signals and the last triggered fallback reason. small timeline UI.
Alex Kim: +1 on timeline. also need audit trail: who edited policy + when. Rolling back should be one-click to prior policy.
Priya Rao: on CB tuning: cb should consider both error-rate and latency spikes. we had a noisy noise issue last week where latency jumped but error rate stayed low, and fallback never triggered because our cb algorithm only looked at 5xxs.
Marco Díaz: yes. propose cb triggers when either: error_rate_pct > threshold OR p95_latency_ms > threshold for N consecutive windows. can keep `cb` object like: `{error_rate_pct: 5, p95_ms: 400, consecutive: 3}`.
Alex Kim: operational question: are CBs evaluated at the routing gateway (fast path) or by an async controller that updates routing rules? tradeoffs: fast detection vs consistency.
Priya Rao: prefer hybrid: local fast-path checks for obvious failures (node down, 5xx spike) and controller for aggregated SLOs (rolling p95). fast-path can immediately divert to next candidate, controller can materialize durable fallback for longer outages.
Jen Liu: good separation. console should show whether fallback is ephemeral (fast-path) vs persistent (controller-applied).
Marco Díaz: telemetry/alerts: make sure we emit `routing.fallback.trigger` with metadata: tier, region, from_model, to_model, reason, duration. then alerting rules for ops on gold-tier global fallbacks.
Alex Kim: agree. also need cost tagging: if fallback increases token cost or moves to a pricier region we should annotate charge implications in audit.
Priya Rao: implementation note: model-variant compatibility matrix must be validated before routing (i.e. function signatures, tokenizer). fallback list should only include compatible models.
ops-bot: [policy-lint] found 1 issue in staging: `fallback: other-region` ambiguous, please qualify region.
Alex Kim: thanks bot. Priya please add validation: fallback entries must be fully-qualified (model:variant@region).
Priya Rao: will do. I'll update the schema and push a small change to the console to show the parsed effective fallback list.
Jen Liu: for rollout UX: when creating a policy change allow a canary rollout to a small % of traffic for N minutes, auto-promote if SLOs stable, auto-rollback if cb fires.
Marco Díaz: prefer percent-based canary with tie to concrete capacity buckets (reserved vs burst) to avoid overload.
Alex Kim: ok action items: 1) Priya -> update DSL schema + add lints (due EOD) 2) Marco -> telemetry events spec and alert rules (tomorrow) 3) Jen -> console mockups for timeline + canary flow (Thursday) 4) me -> design fast-path vs controller handoff doc (Friday).
Jen Liu: I'll include sample mock screenshots and a tiny playbook snippet for on-call.
Priya Rao: pushing schema PR now: https://git.redwood/policies/pull/314
Marco Díaz: filing alert RFC: https://docs.redwood/internal/alerts/routing-fallbacks.md
Alex Kim: thanks all. let's sync 30m after PR merge if needed. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [ci] policy-tests passed on staging.
Priya Rao: merged. marking as in-progress for console changes.
Jen Liu: noted, will prototype after lunch.
